title: Commands: show and list with --json
lead:
`adj show ID` and `adj list [--status S] [--tag T] [--key K]`, each with
`--json`.
findings_note: PROJECT.md v1 feature tier; Milestone 2; acceptance (--json)
boundary: **Not in this slice:** inbox, check and context.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Agents and the owner need to read records; every read command needs `--json`
with a stable shape (acceptance criteria).

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/query/filter.go` and `internal/query/filter_test.go`.
- `internal/render/text.go`, `internal/render/json.go` and
  `internal/render/render_test.go`.
- `internal/commands/show.go` and `internal/commands/list.go`.
- `internal/cli/show_list_test.go`.
- `docs/json.md`: the `--json` shapes of `show` and `list`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
End-to-end CLI tests call `cli.Run` in a fresh `t.TempDir()` store (with
`t.Chdir`, which rules out `t.Parallel`, or a root option the implementer adds
and records under C32), with a fixed clock where dates matter.

- `show ID` prints every set field and the history; `show ID --json` prints
  the record with the keys documented in `docs/json.md`; an unknown ID exits
  non-zero.
- `list` filters by status, tag and key, singly and combined (table-driven in
  `filter_test.go`); results are ordered by ID.
- An invalid `--status` value is a usage error.
- The `--json` output of both commands is byte-identical across two runs and
  ends with a newline.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Filtering in `query` as pure functions over `[]model.Record`; output in
   `render` (JSON through `json.Encoder` with `SetEscapeHTML(false)` and
   two-space indent).
2. Implementer decides and records (C32): the `list --json` top-level shape
   (for example a bare array or `{"records": [...]}`), whether `--tag` repeats,
   and how combined filters combine (proposed: AND).
3. Document both shapes in `docs/json.md`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Run from the repo root after `. scripts/env.sh` (the in-repo cache env, C33;
use the equivalent AGENTS.md names if S02 chose another):

- `go test ./...` passes, including this slice's new tests.
- `go vet ./...` reports nothing.
- `gofmt -l cmd internal` prints nothing (not `gofmt -l .`, which also walks
  `.cache/` and `.worktrees/`).
- Each interface choice made in this slice is a slicer catalog decision with a
  one-line reason (C32).
- `slicer check --json` is clean.
